review_type: Line-by-line mathematical review; no new Monte Carlo or numerical design experiment
claim_reviewed: For A=1/2 and B^2+C^2<=1/4, the continuous-angle oracle KL design value equals Phi(2C), achieved by the equally weighted reflected PSR pair, with the affine null a=1/2 and b=B*atanh(2C)/(2C) for 0<|2C|<1.

checks.reason: rho=(I+beta Z+gamma X)/2 is positive semidefinite with unit trace exactly when beta^2+gamma^2<=1. Tr(rho P_x) reproduces the stated Bernoulli probability. No additional measurement resource is introduced by the proof.

checks.item: Strict feasibility of the proposed null
checks.reason: The derivative proof of atanh(t)<t/sqrt(1-t^2) for 0<t<1 is correct. Combined with |beta|<=sqrt(1-gamma^2), it gives |beta*lambda|<1 and hence sigma>0, trace(sigma)=1, and all null probabilities strictly between zero and one.

In the X eigenbasis, the diagonal entries of Dlog(H*)[rho] are 1/2; the off-diagonal entries are beta*lambda/2. The divided difference is atanh(gamma)/gamma, also for negative gamma. Thus the derivative is exactly sigma and Tr(sigma H*)=1.

The integral formula for Dlog is self-adjoint for the trace inner product. The displayed second directional derivative is negative semidefinite since R E R E R is positive semidefinite. Tr(rho log H) is concave even when rho is singular, so its derivative at positive H* yields the required global supporting inequality.

For interior p, H_x has eigenvalues p/q and (1-p)/(1-q), is positive, has Tr(sigma H_x)=1, and Tr(rho log H_x)=kl(p||q). The supporting linear term vanishes and Tr(rho log H*) equals Phi(gamma). This is a single physical affine null bounding every angle.

The proof never requires rho>0. For p=0 or p=1, (H_x+epsilon I)/(1+epsilon) remains positive and normalized under sigma. The zero-probability eigenspace has zero rho weight; the trace-log limit therefore gives the standard boundary Bernoulli KL.

checks.item: Matching primal lower bound without a minimax exchange
checks.reason: Under the two PSR angles the affine null is the common probability a. Equal weighting makes the a-dependent term -log(a)/2-log(1-a)/2, minimized at a=1/2. The feasible choice b=0 attains Phi(gamma). The separately constructed uniform upper bound proves equality without requiring an interchange of sup and inf.

checks.item: Extension to the opposite-sign physical null
checks.reason: For C>0, any full null with c<=0 has q_plus<=q_minus. At q_plus=q_minus=1/2, the equal-weight KL gradient is (-2C,2C), and its dot product with every feasible displacement is 2C*(q_minus-q_plus)>=0. Convexity proves the same minimum. The c=0 dual remains feasible in the larger null. Negative C follows by reflection.

At C=0 the true law is in the null and the value is zero, including |B|=1/2. At |C|=1/2 physicality forces B=0; the constant null 1/2 gives the log(2) upper bound and the PSR pair attains it. No undefined zero-times-infinite expression is used. Evenness and the signed derivative computation handle negative C.

The document restricts the result to A=1/2, oracle KL information under equal per-query cost. It does not claim a result for general A, finite-prior growth, paid learning, finite-sample stopping cost, SOTA superiority, or mathematical novelty.

limitations: This is an independent human-readable mathematical review, not verification by a formal proof assistant.
The general A!=1/2 reflected-two-angle conjecture remains unresolved.
